problem: Find a basis of $\,\text{Ker}(T)$ given that $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}3y-6z-6x \\ -4y+x+z \\ 2y+8z+8x\end{aligned}].$

activity_context.topic_title: The Kernel of a Linear Transformation

feedback.problem: Find a basis of $\,\text{Ker}(T)$ given that $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}4x-2y \\ -6x+3y\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
Finding the kernel of $\,T\,$ is equivalent to finding the null space of the standard matrix of $\,T.$

For the given linear transformation, the standard matrix is $T=[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -6 & 3\end{aligned}].$ 

Setting $x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],$ we then need to solve the equation $Tx=0.$ First, we reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ -6 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{6}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variable is $x$, and we have one free variable, $y.$ That means we need to find $x$ in terms of $y.$

From the first equation, we get 

$$
x=\frac{1}{2}y.
$$

  

Therefore, if $x\in \text{Ker}(T),$ then 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}y \\ y\end{aligned}]=y[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,y\in R.
$$

This implies that $B={[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$ is a basis of $\text{Ker}(T).$
